title: Mohawk Airlines 405

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board
agencies.report_title: Aircraft Accident Report - Mohawk Airlines Flight 405

location.name: Albany, New York, house 3.5 miles south of airport

summary: Mohawk Airlines Flight 405 crashed into a house in Albany on March 3, 1972. The left propeller was stuck in cruise pitch lock and could not be feathered, creating asymmetric drag. The crew descended below prescribed minimum altitudes while preoccupied with troubleshooting the propeller problem. The aircraft descended uncontrollably and crashed. Of 48 occupants and 1 house resident, 17 were killed.
probable_cause: The crew inability to feather the left propeller in combination with descent below prescribed minimum altitudes for the approach. The Board was unable to determine why the propeller could not be feathered or why the crew failed to effect the standard feathering procedure.

factors.evidence: The left propeller was stuck in cruise pitch lock and could not be feathered (p. 24)
The flight crew descended below prescribed minimum altitudes for the approach (p. 32)
Weather at airport was ceiling indefinite 1,200 feet obscured with 2 miles visibility in light snow (p. 1)
The left propeller creating high asymmetric drag resulted in uncontrollable descent (p. 24)
The aircraft crashed into a house 3.5 miles south of runway (p. 1)

events.text: Flight originated in New York City for final approach to Albany airport runway 01
At 8.5 miles from airport, flight crew reported left propeller was hung up in cruise pitch lock
At about 5 miles out, crew notified Approach Control they were attempting emergency feathering and would land short
Left propeller creating high asymmetric drag; right engine at full power could not arrest uncontrollable descent; aircraft crashed into house 3.5 miles south of runway

recommendations.text: Conduct comprehensive review of propeller feathering procedures and emergency training
Require installation and use of shoulder harnesses for cockpit crew members

safety_changes: Enhanced training on crew resource management and task prioritization during emergencies
Installation of shoulder harnesses in cockpit crews
